content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values when historical mean is high (e.g., >73), and overestimates when mean is low (e.g., <70).
- Underreacts to sudden price spikes; model often fails to capture the full magnitude of upward moves.
- Overreacts to minor price corrections; model sometimes overshoots downward moves.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — model often holds onto overestimated values longer than true price reverts.
- Horizon-specific: last 5–7 days of forecast are most prone to overestimation, especially when true price is trending up.
